clue1: It is a transcontinental country in northeast Africa, with the Sinai Peninsula in Asia, bordered by the Mediterranean and Red Seas.
clue2: Its ancient civilization along the Nile produced pharaohs such as Tutankhamun and Ramses II.
clue3: The Great Sphinx and the Great Pyramid at Giza are among its most famous landmarks.

clue1: It is a coastal country in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, bordered by Benin to the west and Cameroon to the east.
clue2: It is the most populous country in Africa and a major oil producer, with Lagos as its largest city.
clue3: Its film industry, nicknamed Nollywood, is one of the largest in the world by number of films produced.

clue1: It sits at the southern tip of the continent and completely surrounds the small kingdom of Lesotho.
clue2: It ended a system of racial segregation called apartheid and elected Nelson Mandela as president in 1994.
clue3: It has three capital cities and is home to Table Mountain and Kruger National Park.

clue1: It is an East African country straddling the equator, with an Indian Ocean coastline and a share of Lake Victoria.
clue2: It is famed for long-distance runners such as Eliud Kipchoge, who ran a marathon in under two hours in 2019 in a specially arranged event.
clue3: Each year, wildebeest herds cross the Mara River into its Maasai Mara reserve during the Great Migration.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in the Horn of Africa, bordering Eritrea, Djibouti, Somalia and Kenya.
clue2: It defeated an Italian invasion at the Battle of Adwa in 1896, preserving its independence during the Scramble for Africa.
clue3: It is widely believed to be the birthplace of coffee and is home to the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela.

clue1: It is a North African kingdom with coastlines on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea, just across the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain.
clue2: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859, is often called the oldest continuously operating university in the world.
clue3: The blue-washed streets of Chefchaouen and the bustling Jemaa el-Fnaa square in Marrakech are among its iconic sights.

clue1: It is the largest country in Africa by area, with a long Mediterranean coastline and much of the Sahara Desert inside its borders.
clue2: It won independence from France in 1962 after a war of about eight years.
clue3: The Tassili n'Ajjer plateau in its Sahara holds thousands of prehistoric rock paintings and engravings.

clue1: It is the northernmost country in Africa, with a Mediterranean coastline and borders with Algeria and Libya.
clue2: Its ancient city of Carthage was a Phoenician power that fought Rome in the Punic Wars.
clue3: A town in its south, Tataouine, lent its name to Luke Skywalker's home planet in Star Wars, and scenes were filmed nearby.

clue1: It is a West African country on the Gulf of Guinea, bordered by Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso and Togo.
clue2: In 1957 it became the first Sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from European colonial rule, led by Kwame Nkrumah.
clue3: It is known for colorful kente cloth and is home to Lake Volta, one of the world's largest reservoirs by surface area.

clue1: It is an East African country with an Indian Ocean coastline, sharing Lake Victoria, Lake Tanganyika and Lake Malawi with its neighbors.
clue2: It was formed in 1964 through the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.
clue3: It is home to Africa's highest peak, Mount Kilimanjaro, and the vast Serengeti plains.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in East Africa that borders Kenya, South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda and Tanzania.
clue2: Its Bwindi Impenetrable Forest shelters roughly half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas.
clue3: Jinja, on the shore of Lake Victoria, is known as a source of the Nile.

clue1: It is a small, hilly landlocked country in East-Central Africa, bordered by Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
clue2: It holds a nationwide monthly community work day called Umuganda and has banned non-biodegradable plastic bags since 2008.
clue3: It is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Hills' and shelters mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park.

clue1: It is a large island nation in the Indian Ocean off the southeast coast of Africa, separated from the mainland by the Mozambique Channel.
clue2: Roughly 90 percent of its wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth, including more than 100 species of lemur.
clue3: Its Avenue of the Baobabs and the jagged stone forests of the Tsingy are iconic natural landmarks.

clue1: It occupies the westernmost tip of mainland Africa, on the Atlantic coast, and nearly surrounds The Gambia.
clue2: Its capital, Dakar, lent its name to the famous off-road rally that for years finished there after starting in Paris.
clue3: Lake Retba, also called Lac Rose, has pink waters thanks to salt-loving algae.

clue1: It is a North African country with a long Mediterranean coastline, bordered by Egypt, Sudan, Chad, Niger, Algeria and Tunisia.
clue2: Its ruler Muammar Gaddafi held power for 42 years until the 2011 uprising.
clue3: The ancient Roman ruins of Leptis Magna, a UNESCO World Heritage site, stand on its Mediterranean coast.

clue1: It is a large northeast African country with a Red Sea coastline, bordering Egypt, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Chad.
clue2: The ancient Kingdom of Kush, based here, ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty and built more than 200 pyramids.
clue3: Its capital sits where the Blue Nile and the White Nile join to form the main Nile.

clue1: It is a sparsely populated country on the Atlantic coast of southwestern Africa, bordered by Angola, Zambia, Botswana and South Africa.
clue2: It gained independence from South African rule in 1990 after a long struggle.
clue3: Its Skeleton Coast, the towering red dunes of Sossusvlei and the dead trees of Deadvlei are iconic desert scenes.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in southern Africa bordered by Namibia, Zambia, Zimbabwe and South Africa.
clue2: It is one of the world's leading diamond producers and is often cited as one of Africa's most stable democracies.
clue3: The Okavango Delta, an inland delta that floods each year, is a wildlife haven here.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in southern Africa, located between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers.
clue2: The medieval stone ruins of a trading city, a UNESCO site, gave the modern country its name.
clue3: It shares the thundering Victoria Falls, known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya, with its northern neighbor Zambia.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in southern Africa, north of the Zambezi River, bordering Tanzania, Malawi, Zimbabwe and Angola.
clue2: Its Copperbelt region makes copper the country's leading export.
clue3: On the side of Victoria Falls near Livingstone, visitors can swim in 'Devil's Pool', a natural rock pool at the edge of the drop.

clue1: It is a large landlocked country in West Africa, stretching from the Sahara in the north to the Niger River basin in the south.
clue2: Its medieval emperor Mansa Musa, who made a famous pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324, is often described as one of the richest people in history.
clue3: The Great Mosque of Djenne is often called the largest mud-brick building in the world, and the fabled city of Timbuktu lies here.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in West Africa, roughly four-fifths covered by the Sahara, with Chad to the east and Algeria and Libya to the north.
clue2: It is one of the world's significant sources of uranium.
clue3: Its Tenere desert once held a lone acacia thought to be the most isolated tree on Earth, until a truck knocked it down in 1973.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in north-central Africa, bordered by Libya, Sudan, Niger and Cameroon.
clue2: A large shallow lake shared with Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria, which gave the country its name, has shrunk by roughly 90 percent since the 1960s.
clue3: The Ennedi Plateau, with its sandstone arches and rock art, and the Ounianga lakes in the Sahara are UNESCO-listed.

clue1: It is the largest country in Sub-Saharan Africa, with a very short Atlantic coastline and territory straddling the equator.
clue2: Africa's second-longest river flows through it, and its forests form the second-largest continuous tropical rainforest in the world.
clue3: It is the only country where wild bonobos live, and its Virunga National Park shelters mountain gorillas.

clue1: It is a country on the southwest Atlantic coast of Africa, bordered by Namibia, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and includes the exclave of Cabinda.
clue2: It won independence from Portugal in 1975 and then endured a civil war that lasted until 2002.
clue3: Its Kalandula Falls rank among the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume.

clue1: It is a country on Africa's southeast coast with a long Indian Ocean shoreline, bordered by Tanzania, Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Eswatini and South Africa.
clue2: It is one of the few African countries with Portuguese as its official language, having gained independence from Portugal in 1975.
clue3: The Bazaruto Archipelago, with its islands, dunes, coral reefs and dugongs, is a marine national park here.

clue1: It is a country on the Gulf of Guinea where West and Central Africa meet, bordered by Nigeria, Chad and Gabon among others.
clue2: Its national football team, the Indomitable Lions, became the first African side to reach a World Cup quarterfinal, in 1990.
clue3: Its varied landscapes, from beaches to rainforest to savanna, earn it the nickname 'Africa in miniature'.

clue1: It is a country in the Horn of Africa with a long Red Sea coastline, bordered by Sudan, Ethiopia and Djibouti.
clue2: It gained formal independence from Ethiopia in 1993 after a referendum, following a decades-long war.
clue3: Its capital's Art Deco and modernist Italian colonial buildings earned UNESCO World Heritage status in 2017.

clue1: It is a small country in the Horn of Africa on the Gulf of Aden, at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.
clue2: Its strategic location hosts military bases of several foreign countries, including the United States, France, China and Japan.
clue3: Lake Assal in its interior is one of the saltiest lakes in the world and the lowest point in Africa.

clue1: It is a small landlocked kingdom entirely surrounded by a single neighbor, South Africa.
clue2: It is known as the 'Kingdom in the Sky' because its entire territory lies above 1,000 meters in elevation.
clue3: Its national flag features a traditional conical straw hat.

clue1: It is a small landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, bordered by South Africa and Mozambique.
clue2: It is one of the world's last absolute monarchies, ruled by King Mswati III.
clue3: Each year thousands of young women take part in the Umhlanga Reed Dance festival.

clue1: It is an archipelago of about 115 islands in the western Indian Ocean, northeast of Madagascar.
clue2: Its Vallee de Mai is home to the coco de mer, a palm that produces the world's largest seed.
clue3: Granite boulders and the pink-tinged sands of Anse Source d'Argent on La Digue are iconic sights.

clue1: It is an island nation in the Indian Ocean, east of Madagascar and near Reunion.
clue2: It was the only known home of the dodo, a flightless bird driven to extinction in the 17th century.
clue3: An underwater 'waterfall' illusion off Le Morne Brabant and the Seven Coloured Earths of Chamarel are famous sights.

clue1: It is a narrow landlocked country in southeast Africa, bordered by Zambia, Tanzania and Mozambique.
clue2: A vast lake, home to hundreds of species of cichlid fish, runs along much of its eastern border.
clue3: It is nicknamed the 'Warm Heart of Africa'.

clue1: It spans East Asia and shares land borders with 14 countries, including India, Russia, Mongolia and Vietnam.
clue2: It invented paper, printing, gunpowder and the compass, known as the Four Great Inventions.
clue3: The Great Wall and the Terracotta Army near Xi'an are among its famous landmarks, and giant pandas are its national symbol.

clue1: It is the largest country in South Asia, bordered by Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar.
clue2: It is the world's most populous country and the birthplace of Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism.
clue3: The Taj Mahal, built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, is its most iconic monument, and Diwali, the festival of lights, is widely celebrated.

clue1: It is an island nation in East Asia in the Pacific Ocean, made up of four main islands: Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu and Shikoku.
clue2: It opened the world's first high-speed rail network, the Shinkansen bullet train, in 1964.
clue3: Mount Fuji, cherry blossoms and sushi are among its most recognizable symbols.

clue1: It occupies the southern half of a peninsula in East Asia, bordered by the Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan.
clue2: Its cultural exports, including K-pop and the film Parasite, which won the Best Picture Oscar in 2020, have gained worldwide popularity.
clue3: It is famous for the fermented cabbage dish kimchi, and its alphabet Hangul was created in the 15th century under King Sejong.

clue1: It occupies the northern half of an East Asian peninsula and borders China and Russia.
clue2: It has been ruled by three generations of the Kim family since 1948.
clue3: A heavily fortified Demilitarized Zone, with the truce village of Panmunjom, divides it from its southern neighbor.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in East Asia sandwiched between Russia and China.
clue2: It was the heart of an empire founded by Genghis Khan in 1206 that became the largest contiguous land empire in history.
clue3: Many of its people live as nomads in round felt tents called gers, and the annual Naadam festival features wrestling, archery and horse racing.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in South Asia, in the Himalayas between China and India.
clue2: It is home to eight of the world's ten highest mountains, including Mount Everest on its border.
clue3: Its flag is the only national flag in the world that is not rectangular.

clue1: It is a small landlocked Himalayan kingdom in South Asia, between China and India.
clue2: It measures national progress using 'Gross National Happiness' rather than only GDP.
clue3: The Tiger's Nest monastery, Paro Taktsang, clings to a cliff high above a valley here.

clue1: It is a low-lying country in South Asia on the Bay of Bengal, almost entirely surrounded by India, with a short border with Myanmar.
clue2: It gained independence in 1971 after a war of liberation from Pakistan.
clue3: It shares the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, with India, and the forest is a home of the Royal Bengal tiger.

clue1: It is a teardrop-shaped island nation in the Indian Ocean, just off the southern tip of India.
clue2: It is one of the world's largest exporters of tea, grown on hill-country plantations.
clue3: The rock fortress of Sigiriya and the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy, said to house a tooth relic of the Buddha, are famous sites.

clue1: It is a country in South Asia bordering India, Afghanistan, Iran and China, with a coast on the Arabian Sea.
clue2: The ruins of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization city of Mohenjo-daro lie within its borders.
clue3: It is home to K2, the second-highest mountain in the world.

clue1: It is a landlocked, mountainous country in Central and South Asia, bordered by Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and China.
clue2: It has earned the nickname 'Graveyard of Empires' for wearing down invading powers, including Britain and the Soviet Union.
clue3: The Bamiyan valley once held giant Buddha statues carved into a cliff, which were destroyed in 2001.

clue1: It is a large country in Southwest Asia with coasts on the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf.
clue2: It was the center of the ancient Persian Empire, founded by Cyrus the Great.
clue3: The ruins of Persepolis and the celebration of Nowruz, the Persian New Year, are iconic.

clue1: It is a Middle Eastern country watered by the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, with a short coast on the Persian Gulf.
clue2: Ancient Mesopotamia, where cuneiform writing and the first cities such as Ur arose, lay within its borders.
clue3: The Hanging Gardens, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, were said to have been in its ancient city of Babylon.

clue1: It occupies most of a large desert peninsula in Southwest Asia, with coasts on the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.
clue2: It is the birthplace of Islam and home to its two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina.
clue3: It holds some of the world's largest oil reserves, and the Empty Quarter, the largest continuous sand desert on Earth, covers its south.

clue1: It straddles two continents, with territory in both Europe and Asia separated by the Bosphorus strait.
clue2: The Ottoman Empire, which conquered Constantinople in 1453, was based here, and that city is now called Istanbul.
clue3: Cappadocia's fairy chimneys and hot-air balloons, and the white terraces of Pamukkale, are iconic landscapes.

clue1: It lies on the eastern Mediterranean coast in the Middle East, bordered by Lebanon, Syria, Jordan and Egypt.
clue2: Founded as a modern state in 1948, it contains Jerusalem, whose holy sites are sacred to Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
clue3: It borders the Dead Sea, whose shore is the lowest point on land on Earth.

clue1: It is a kingdom in the Middle East bordered by Syria, Iraq, Saudi Arabia and Israel, with a short Red Sea coastline at Aqaba.
clue2: It is home to the rose-red ancient Nabataean city of Petra, carved into sandstone cliffs.
clue3: The red desert landscape of Wadi Rum, nicknamed the Valley of the Moon, has appeared in films such as Lawrence of Arabia and The Martian.

clue1: It is a small country on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean, between Syria and Israel.
clue2: Its ancient Phoenician cities, such as Byblos and Tyre, helped spread an early alphabet across the Mediterranean.
clue3: A cedar tree is the emblem on its flag, and its Roman temples at Baalbek are UNESCO-listed.

clue1: It is a country at the southwestern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, with coasts on the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, bordered by Saudi Arabia and Oman.
clue2: The ancient walled city of Shibam, known as the 'Manhattan of the Desert', has mud-brick skyscrapers.
clue3: The remote island of Socotra, with its otherworldly dragon blood trees, belongs to it.

clue1: It is a country on the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, with a long coastline on the Arabian Sea, bordering Yemen, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
clue2: It was long a seafaring trading power whose sultans once ruled Zanzibar.
clue3: It is famed for frankincense from the Dhofar region and for the towering Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque in Muscat.

clue1: It is a federation of seven sheikhdoms on the southeastern Arabian Peninsula, on the Persian Gulf, bordered by Saudi Arabia and Oman.
clue2: Its economy grew from oil and trade, and Abu Dhabi and Dubai are its leading cities.
clue3: Dubai's Burj Khalifa, at 828 meters, is the tallest building in the world.

clue1: It is a small peninsula country jutting into the Persian Gulf, sharing its only land border with Saudi Arabia.
clue2: It hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first held in the Middle East.
clue3: It is one of the world's largest exporters of liquefied natural gas, and its capital, Doha, is home to the Al Jazeera network.

clue1: It is the world's largest landlocked country, stretching from the Caspian Sea to the Altai Mountains in Central Asia.
clue2: It hosts the Baikonur Cosmodrome, the world's first and largest space launch facility, where Yuri Gagarin was launched in 1961.
clue3: Its capital's Bayterek Tower and the tent-shaped Khan Shatyr shopping center are futuristic landmarks.

clue1: It is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world, in Central Asia.
clue2: Its Silk Road cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva are renowned for their blue-tiled Islamic architecture.
clue3: It borders the Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, which has shrunk dramatically and is shared with Kazakhstan.

clue1: It is a mountainous, landlocked country in Central Asia, bordered by Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and China.
clue2: Its nomadic heritage is celebrated in the World Nomad Games and in the epic poem Manas.
clue3: Issyk-Kul, a huge saline mountain lake whose name means 'warm lake', rarely freezes in winter.

clue1: It is a mountainous landlocked country in Central Asia, bordered by Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and China.
clue2: More than 90 percent of its territory is mountainous, including much of the Pamir range, sometimes called the 'Roof of the World'.
clue3: Fedchenko Glacier, the longest glacier outside the polar regions, is located here.

clue1: It is a Central Asian country on the eastern shore of the Caspian Sea, bordered by Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Afghanistan and Iran.
clue2: About 70 percent of its land is covered by the Karakum Desert.
clue3: The Darvaza gas crater, nicknamed the 'Door to Hell', has been burning in the desert for decades.

clue1: It is a country in mainland Southeast Asia bordered by Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia and Malaysia, with coastlines on the Andaman Sea and the South China Sea.
clue2: It is the only Southeast Asian nation never colonized by a European power.
clue3: It is famed for golden Buddhist temples such as Wat Arun, floating markets, elephants and spicy dishes like tom yum soup and green curry.

clue1: It is an S-shaped country in Southeast Asia along the South China Sea, bordered by China, Laos and Cambodia.
clue2: It fought a long war against the United States that ended in 1975 with the fall of Saigon.
clue3: The limestone islands of Ha Long Bay and dishes such as pho and banh mi are iconic.

clue1: It is the only landlocked country in mainland Southeast Asia, bordered by China, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand and Myanmar.
clue2: Its former royal capital, Luang Prabang, is a UNESCO World Heritage town known for saffron-robed monks receiving alms at dawn.
clue3: The Plain of Jars, with thousands of mysterious ancient stone jars, is a UNESCO World Heritage site here.

clue1: It is a Southeast Asian country on the Gulf of Thailand, bordered by Thailand, Laos and Vietnam.
clue2: It was the center of the Khmer Empire, which flourished from the 9th to the 15th century.
clue3: Angkor Wat, the world's largest religious monument, appears on its national flag.

clue1: It is the largest country in mainland Southeast Asia, bordered by Bangladesh, India, China, Laos and Thailand, with a long coastline on the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.
clue2: Its ancient capital, Bagan, has thousands of Buddhist temples and pagodas scattered across a dry plain.
clue3: The gold-covered Shwedagon Pagoda glitters above its largest city, Yangon.

clue1: It is split between a peninsula in Southeast Asia and part of the island of Borneo, separated by the South China Sea.
clue2: Its Petronas Twin Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.
clue3: Its rainforests shelter orangutans, and the Rafflesia, the world's largest single flower, grows on Borneo.

clue1: It is a tiny island city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, just off the coast of Malaysia.
clue2: It became independent in 1965 after separating from Malaysia and grew into one of the world's busiest ports.
clue3: Its Marina Bay Sands hotel, with a rooftop infinity pool, and the 'Supertrees' of Gardens by the Bay are iconic.

clue1: It is the world's largest archipelagic country, spanning more than 17,000 islands across the equator between Asia and Australia.
clue2: It has the largest Muslim population of any country in the world.
clue3: The Komodo dragon, the world's largest living lizard, roams its islands, and the Buddhist temple of Borobudur stands on Java.

clue1: It is an archipelago of more than 7,000 islands in Southeast Asia between the South China Sea and the Pacific Ocean.
clue2: It was a Spanish colony for more than 300 years and is a predominantly Catholic country.
clue3: The Chocolate Hills of Bohol, the Banaue Rice Terraces and the tiny tarsier are famous.

clue1: It is an island nation of coral atolls in the Indian Ocean, southwest of Sri Lanka and India.
clue2: It is the lowest-lying country in the world, with an average natural ground level about 1.5 meters above sea level, making it vulnerable to rising seas.
clue3: It is famous for luxury resorts on private islands and for overwater bungalows.

clue1: It is a country in the Caucasus at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, on the eastern Black Sea coast, bordered by Russia, Turkey, Armenia and Azerbaijan.
clue2: It is considered one of the oldest wine-producing regions, with an 8,000-year tradition of fermenting wine in clay vessels called qvevri.
clue3: It has a unique curvy alphabet unlike any other script, and its national dish is khachapuri, a cheese-filled bread often shaped like a boat.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in the South Caucasus, bordered by Georgia, Azerbaijan, Iran and Turkey.
clue2: According to tradition, it became the first country to adopt Christianity as its state religion, in 301 AD.
clue3: Mount Ararat, a national symbol, is visible from its capital, Yerevan, though the peak lies just across the border.

clue1: It is a country in the South Caucasus on the western shore of the Caspian Sea, bordered by Russia, Georgia, Armenia and Iran.
clue2: Its capital, Baku, was one of the world's earliest oil-drilling centers, and an oil boom shaped the late 19th century here.
clue3: It is nicknamed the 'Land of Fire', and natural gas flames burn continuously on the hillside of Yanar Dag.

clue1: It is a tiny sultanate on the northern coast of the island of Borneo, surrounded on land by Malaysia.
clue2: It is one of the wealthiest countries in the world thanks to oil and natural gas, and is ruled by a sultan.
clue3: Kampong Ayer, a centuries-old 'water village' of houses on stilts, lies on the river in its capital.

clue1: It is a Western European country with coasts on the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea, bordering Spain, Italy, Germany and Belgium.
clue2: It was the site of the 1789 revolution that overthrew its monarchy.
clue3: Its capital has the Eiffel Tower, and it is renowned for croissants, baguettes and cheese.

clue1: It is a Central European country with coastlines on the North and Baltic Seas, bordered by nine neighbors including Poland, France and Austria.
clue2: It was divided into East and West after World War II and reunified in 1990, following the fall of the Berlin Wall.
clue3: It is famous for Oktoberfest in Munich and for stretches of autobahn with no general speed limit.

clue1: It is a boot-shaped peninsula in Southern Europe extending into the Mediterranean, with Sicily and Sardinia as its largest islands.
clue2: It was the heart of the Roman Empire and the birthplace of the Renaissance.
clue3: The Colosseum, the Leaning Tower of Pisa, pizza and gelato are iconic.

clue1: It occupies most of the Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe, bordering Portugal, France and Andorra.
clue2: It is the birthplace of artists such as Picasso and Dali and of the classic novel Don Quixote.
clue3: Gaudi's Sagrada Familia in Barcelona, flamenco, paella and the running of the bulls in Pamplona are iconic.

clue1: It is the westernmost country of mainland Europe, on the Iberian Peninsula, and its only land neighbor is Spain.
clue2: Its explorers, including Vasco da Gama, pioneered sea routes to India during the Age of Discovery.
clue3: It is known for pastel de nata custard tarts, mournful fado music and decorative blue tiles called azulejos.

clue1: It is an island nation off the northwest coast of continental Europe, made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
clue2: It was the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution and once ruled the largest empire in history.
clue3: Big Ben, Stonehenge and afternoon tea are among its icons.

clue1: It occupies about five-sixths of an island in the North Atlantic, to the west of Great Britain.
clue2: A potato famine in the 1840s led to mass emigration, and it produced writers such as James Joyce, W. B. Yeats and Samuel Beckett.
clue3: St Patrick's Day, shamrocks, Guinness stout and the Cliffs of Moher are iconic.

clue1: It is a volcanic island nation in the North Atlantic, just south of the Arctic Circle, between Greenland and Norway.
clue2: Its parliament, the Althing, founded in 930, is one of the oldest in the world.
clue3: Geysers, glaciers, the Northern Lights and the Blue Lagoon geothermal spa are iconic.

clue1: It lies on the western side of the Scandinavian Peninsula, with a long coastline of deep fjords along the North Atlantic.
clue2: It awards the Nobel Peace Prize in its capital, Oslo, and holds a huge sovereign wealth fund built on oil revenue.
clue3: Vikings once sailed from its shores, and it is a top place to see the midnight sun and the aurora borealis.

clue1: It is a Scandinavian country in Northern Europe, bordered by Norway and Finland, with a long Baltic Sea coastline.
clue2: Alfred Nobel, inventor of dynamite, was born here, and the Nobel Prize ceremony is held in its capital.
clue3: IKEA furniture, the pop group ABBA and the tradition of 'fika' coffee breaks are iconic.

clue1: It is a Nordic country in northern Europe, bordered by Sweden, Norway and Russia, with thousands of lakes.
clue2: It has topped the World Happiness Report ranking for several years in a row.
clue3: It is the home of the sauna, and Santa Claus Village at the Arctic Circle in Rovaniemi is a famous attraction.

clue1: It is a Scandinavian country made up of the Jutland peninsula and more than 400 islands, connected to Sweden by the Oresund Bridge.
clue2: It is the home of LEGO and of the fairy-tale writer Hans Christian Andersen.
clue3: Its capital's Little Mermaid statue and the cozy lifestyle concept of 'hygge' are famous, and its territory includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

clue1: It is a low-lying country in Northwestern Europe on the North Sea, with much of its land below sea level, bordered by Germany and Belgium.
clue2: It has a famous system of dikes and canals to keep out the sea, and Amsterdam's canal ring is UNESCO-listed.
clue3: Tulips, windmills, wooden clogs and cycling are iconic.

clue1: It is a small Western European country bordered by France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands, with a short North Sea coast.
clue2: Its capital hosts the headquarters of NATO and the main institutions of the European Union.
clue3: Chocolate pralines, waffles, Trappist beers and the Manneken Pis statue are iconic.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in the heart of Europe, bordered by Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein.
clue2: It has a long tradition of political neutrality and hosts many international organizations in Geneva.
clue3: Chocolate, cheese fondue, precision watches and the Matterhorn are iconic.

clue1: It is a landlocked, mostly Alpine country in Central Europe, bordered by Germany, Italy and Hungary among others.
clue2: Mozart was born in its city of Salzburg, and Vienna was the capital of the Habsburg Empire.
clue3: It is the setting of The Sound of Music and is known for Vienna's waltz and Sachertorte.

clue1: It is a Central European country on the Baltic Sea, bordered by Germany, Czechia, Slovakia, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania and Russia's Kaliningrad exclave.
clue2: Marie Curie, a two-time Nobel laureate, and Nicolaus Copernicus, who proposed the heliocentric model, were born here.
clue3: The Wieliczka Salt Mine near Krakow, with underground chapels carved from salt, is a UNESCO site.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in Central Europe, bordered by Germany, Poland, Slovakia and Austria.
clue2: It separated peacefully from Slovakia in 1993 in the 'Velvet Divorce', after the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
clue3: Its capital, Prague, has a famous Astronomical Clock, and Pilsner beer originated in the city of Plzen.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in Central Europe, centered on the Carpathian Basin, with the Danube flowing through its capital.
clue2: It is the birthplace of the Rubik's Cube, invented by Erno Rubik in 1974.
clue3: Thermal baths such as Szechenyi in its capital and the spicy stew goulash are iconic, and Lake Balaton is the largest lake in Central Europe.

clue1: It is a southeastern European country with thousands of islands in the Aegean and Ionian Seas, at the southern tip of the Balkan Peninsula.
clue2: It is the birthplace of democracy in ancient Athens and of the Olympic Games.
clue3: The Acropolis and Parthenon, whitewashed villages on Santorini, feta cheese and moussaka are iconic.

clue1: It is a country in Southeastern Europe, curved around by the Carpathian Mountains, with a coast on the Black Sea and the Danube delta.
clue2: Its Transylvania region is linked to Vlad the Impaler, a historical figure who partly inspired Bram Stoker's Dracula.
clue3: Its Palace of the Parliament in the capital is one of the largest and heaviest buildings in the world.

clue1: It is a Balkan country in southeastern Europe with a Black Sea coast, bordered by Romania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Greece and Turkey.
clue2: It considers itself the cradle of the Cyrillic alphabet, which was developed at its Preslav Literary School.
clue3: Its Rose Valley produces a large share of the world's rose oil, and there a shake of the head traditionally signals 'yes'.

clue1: It is a Balkan country on the eastern Adriatic coast with more than a thousand islands, bordering Slovenia, Hungary, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro.
clue2: Its coastal city of Dubrovnik, called the Pearl of the Adriatic, is a UNESCO site featured in Game of Thrones.
clue3: The necktie is said to have originated with its 17th-century soldiers, and the turquoise cascades of Plitvice Lakes are iconic.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in the Balkans, where the Sava River meets the Danube at its capital, Belgrade.
clue2: Novak Djokovic, one of the greatest tennis players ever, was born in its capital.
clue3: It hosts the Guca Trumpet Festival and the Exit music festival at the Petrovaradin Fortress.

clue1: It is a large Eastern European country on the northern coast of the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, bordered by Russia, Belarus, Poland and Romania.
clue2: It is known as the 'breadbasket of Europe' for its fertile black soil and huge wheat exports.
clue3: The 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster occurred here, and Kyiv's golden-domed St Sophia Cathedral dates to the 11th century.

clue1: It is the largest country in the world by area, spanning Eastern Europe and northern Asia across eleven time zones.
clue2: Its Trans-Siberian Railway, the longest railway line in the world, links Moscow to Vladivostok.
clue3: Matryoshka nesting dolls and the onion-domed St Basil's Cathedral in Red Square are iconic.

clue1: It is a landlocked Eastern European country bordered by Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia.
clue2: The Bialowieza forest, shared with Poland, is one of Europe's last primeval lowland forests and home to the European bison.
clue3: The UNESCO-listed Mir Castle Complex, a fortress with Gothic and Renaissance elements, stands here.

clue1: It is the northernmost of the three Baltic states, on the Gulf of Finland, bordered by Latvia and Russia.
clue2: It is a digital pioneer, an early adopter of online voting and e-residency and the birthplace of Skype.
clue3: Its capital's medieval Old Town is a UNESCO site, and its 'Singing Revolution' helped it break free from the Soviet Union.

clue1: It is the middle Baltic state, bordered by Estonia, Lithuania, Russia and Belarus, with a coast on the Baltic Sea and the Gulf of Riga.
clue2: Its capital has one of the world's greatest concentrations of Art Nouveau architecture.
clue3: It holds a massive Song and Dance Festival roughly every five years, a tradition on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.

clue1: It is the southernmost and largest Baltic state, bordered by Latvia, Belarus, Poland and Russia's Kaliningrad exclave.
clue2: In 1990 it became the first Soviet republic to declare independence.
clue3: The Hill of Crosses, covered with more than 100,000 crosses, is a pilgrimage site near the city of Siauliai.

clue1: It is a small Alpine country bordering Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia, with a short Adriatic coastline.
clue2: It gained independence from Yugoslavia in 1991 after a ten-day war.
clue3: Lake Bled, with a small island church, and the vast Postojna Cave are iconic sights.

clue1: It is a landlocked Central European country bordered by Poland, Ukraine, Hungary, Austria and the Czech Republic.
clue2: The High Tatras, the highest mountain range in the Carpathians, are within its borders.
clue3: Spis Castle, one of the largest castle complexes in Central Europe, is a UNESCO site here.

clue1: It is a Balkan country on the Adriatic and Ionian Seas, bordered by Montenegro, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Greece.
clue2: It was ruled by an isolationist communist regime under Enver Hoxha until the early 1990s and was left dotted with concrete bunkers.
clue3: The UNESCO-listed city of Berat is nicknamed the 'city of a thousand windows'.

clue1: It is a tiny island nation in the central Mediterranean, south of Sicily and north of Libya.
clue2: The Knights of St John, who withstood the Great Siege of 1565, once ruled the islands.
clue3: Its capital, Valletta, is a UNESCO World Heritage city, and its Ggantija temples are among the oldest freestanding structures in the world.

clue1: It is a tiny landlocked country in Western Europe, bordered by Belgium, France and Germany.
clue2: It is the world's only remaining sovereign grand duchy.
clue3: It is home to European institutions such as the Court of Justice of the European Union and has one of the highest GDPs per capita in the world.

clue1: It is a tiny, doubly landlocked principality in the Alps between Switzerland and Austria.
clue2: It is one of the smallest countries in the world, ruled by a prince whose family holds real political powers.
clue3: Vaduz Castle overlooks the capital and is the residence of the prince.

clue1: It is a tiny principality on the French Riviera, on the Mediterranean coast, surrounded on land by France.
clue2: It hosts a prestigious Formula 1 Grand Prix on narrow city streets.
clue3: It is the world's second-smallest sovereign state and is famous for the casino in Monte Carlo.

clue1: It occupies the central part of North America, stretching from the Atlantic to the Pacific, and also includes Alaska and Hawaii.
clue2: It declared independence from Britain on July 4, 1776, and landed astronauts on the Moon in 1969.
clue3: The Statue of Liberty, a gift from France, and the Grand Canyon are iconic.

clue1: It is the second-largest country in the world by area, occupying the northern part of North America and bordering only one country by land.
clue2: It has two official languages, English and French, and its capital is Ottawa.
clue3: A maple leaf is on its flag, and it is famed for maple syrup, ice hockey and Niagara Falls, which it shares with its southern neighbor.

clue1: It is a country in southern North America, bordered by the United States to the north and Guatemala and Belize to the south, with coasts on the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
clue2: The Aztec capital Tenochtitlan and the Maya pyramids of Chichen Itza were located within its territory.
clue3: Day of the Dead celebrations, tacos, mariachi music and tequila are iconic.

clue1: It is the largest island in the Caribbean, lying just south of Florida.
clue2: Its 1959 revolution, led by Fidel Castro and joined by Che Guevara, brought a communist government to power.
clue3: Havana's streets are full of 1950s American cars, and the island is famed for hand-rolled cigars and salsa music.

clue1: It is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea, south of Cuba.
clue2: It produced Bob Marley and the reggae music genre, and the sprinter Usain Bolt.
clue3: Blue Mountain coffee and jerk chicken are iconic, and the Rastafari movement began here.

clue1: It occupies the western third of the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean, sharing it with the Dominican Republic.
clue2: In 1804 it became the first independent Black-led republic, following a successful slave revolution led by Toussaint Louverture.
clue3: The mountaintop Citadelle Laferriere, a massive fortress built after independence, is one of its landmarks.

clue1: It occupies the eastern two-thirds of the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean, bordering Haiti.
clue2: Its capital, Santo Domingo, is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas.
clue3: Merengue and bachata music and baseball are cultural passions, and the beaches of Punta Cana are iconic.

clue1: It is a narrow Central American country with coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea, between Nicaragua and Panama.
clue2: It abolished its army in 1948 and protects a large share of its land as national parks.
clue3: The phrase 'pura vida', sloths and the cloud forests of Monteverde are iconic.

clue1: It is the southernmost Central American country, linking North and South America, between Costa Rica and Colombia.
clue2: Its canal, opened in 1914, connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
clue3: Its Guna people, based in the San Blas islands, make colorful reverse-appliqué textiles called molas.

clue1: It is a Central American country south of Mexico, with coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
clue2: The ancient Maya city of Tikal, with towering temple pyramids rising above the jungle, is a UNESCO site here.
clue3: Lake Atitlan, ringed by volcanoes, is often called one of the most beautiful lakes in the world.

clue1: It is a Central American country with coasts on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean, bordering Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua.
clue2: The ancient Maya city of Copan, known for its Hieroglyphic Stairway, lies here.
clue3: Its Bay Islands, including Roatan, sit beside the world's second-largest barrier reef system.

clue1: It is a small Central American country on the Caribbean coast, bordered by Mexico and Guatemala.
clue2: It is the only country in Central America with English as its official language.
clue3: The Great Blue Hole, a giant marine sinkhole, lies off its coast within the world's second-largest barrier reef system.

clue1: It is the largest country in Central America, between Honduras and Costa Rica, with coasts on the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
clue2: Its 1979 revolution overthrew the Somoza dynasty and brought the Sandinistas to power.
clue3: The largest lake in Central America lies within it, and it contains Ometepe, an island formed by two volcanoes.

clue1: It is an archipelago of about 700 islands and thousands of cays in the Atlantic Ocean, east of Florida and north of Cuba.
clue2: Christopher Columbus made his first landfall in the Americas in 1492 on one of its islands, traditionally identified as San Salvador.
clue3: It is famous for swimming pigs on the beaches of the Exumas and the pink-sand beaches of Harbour Island.

clue1: It is the easternmost island in the Caribbean, in the Lesser Antilles, east of the Windward Islands.
clue2: It is the birthplace of the singer Rihanna and became a republic in 2021, removing the British monarch as head of state.
clue3: It claims to be the birthplace of rum and is home to Mount Gay, one of the oldest rum brands in the world.

clue1: It is a two-island Caribbean nation just off the northeastern coast of Venezuela, at the southern end of the Lesser Antilles.
clue2: It is the birthplace of the steelpan, often called the only acoustic instrument invented in the 20th century.
clue3: Its pre-Lenten Carnival, with calypso and soca music, is among the Caribbean's biggest festivals, and its Pitch Lake is the largest natural deposit of asphalt.

clue1: It is the largest country in South America, sharing borders with every other country on the continent except Chile and Ecuador.
clue2: It has won the FIFA World Cup five times, more than any other nation.
clue3: Christ the Redeemer overlooks Rio de Janeiro, and the Amazon rainforest and Carnival are iconic.

clue1: It is the second-largest country in South America, stretching from the subtropics to Tierra del Fuego, with Chile along its western border.
clue2: It is the homeland of football stars Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi and won the 2022 World Cup.
clue3: Tango, gaucho cowboys, Patagonian glaciers and the Iguazu Falls, shared with Brazil, are iconic.

clue1: It is a very long, narrow country running along the western edge of South America between the Andes and the Pacific Ocean.
clue2: It is the world's largest producer of copper.
clue3: Easter Island, with its giant moai statues, belongs to it, and its Atacama is the driest non-polar desert on Earth.

clue1: It is a country on the Pacific coast of South America, with the Andes and part of the Amazon rainforest, bordered by Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Bolivia and Chile.
clue2: It was the heart of the Inca Empire, whose capital was Cusco.
clue3: Machu Picchu, the mountaintop citadel, and the giant Nazca Lines are iconic, as are llamas and alpacas.

clue1: It is the only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
clue2: Gabriel Garcia Marquez, author of One Hundred Years of Solitude, was born here.
clue3: Its Cano Cristales, the 'river of five colors', is famous for its vivid aquatic plants.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in west-central South America, bordered by Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Chile and Peru.
clue2: It has two capital cities, La Paz and Sucre, and La Paz is the highest seat of government in the world.
clue3: The Uyuni salt flat, the largest in the world, becomes a giant mirror in the rainy season.

clue1: It is a small South American country on the Pacific coast, straddling the equator and bordered by Colombia and Peru.
clue2: Its Galapagos Islands helped inspire Charles Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection.
clue3: It is one of the world's largest banana exporters, and its capital, Quito, lies at about 2,850 meters above sea level.

clue1: It is a country on the northern coast of South America, bordered by Colombia, Brazil and Guyana, with a long Caribbean coastline.
clue2: It has the world's largest proven oil reserves.
clue3: Angel Falls, the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, drops from a flat-topped mountain in Canaima National Park.

clue1: It is a small South American country on the Atlantic coast and the Rio de la Plata, squeezed between Argentina and Brazil.
clue2: It hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup, in 1930.
clue3: Drinking yerba mate is a national obsession, and 'La Mano', a giant sculpture of a hand emerging from the sand, stands at Punta del Este.

clue1: It is a landlocked country in the heart of South America, between Argentina, Bolivia and Brazil.
clue2: It shares the giant Itaipu hydroelectric dam with Brazil, and Guarani is a co-official language.
clue3: Its national flag is unusual because the front and back have different emblems.

clue1: It is a country on the northeast coast of South America, bordered by Venezuela, Brazil and Suriname.
clue2: It is the only country in South America with English as its official language.
clue3: Kaieteur Falls, one of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls in the world, plunges through its rainforest.

clue1: It is the smallest independent country in South America, on the Atlantic coast between Guyana and French Guiana.
clue2: It is the only country in South America where Dutch is the official language.
clue3: Around 90 percent of its land is covered by rainforest, among the highest forest cover of any country.

clue1: It is both a country and a continent, surrounded by the Indian and Pacific Oceans, and is the sixth-largest country in the world.
clue2: Its Aboriginal peoples maintain one of the world's oldest continuous cultures, stretching back tens of thousands of years.
clue3: Kangaroos, koalas, the Sydney Opera House and the Great Barrier Reef are iconic.

clue1: It is an island nation in the southwest Pacific Ocean, southeast of Australia, made up of two main islands.
clue2: In 1893 it became the first self-governing country to grant women the right to vote in national elections.
clue3: The kiwi bird, the Maori haka war dance and film locations from The Lord of the Rings are iconic.

clue1: It is an archipelago of more than 300 islands in the South Pacific, east of Vanuatu.
clue2: It won its first Olympic gold medal in rugby sevens at the 2016 Games.
clue3: It is known for the traditional yaqona, or kava, ceremony and for luxury island resorts.

clue1: It occupies the eastern half of the world's second-largest island, along with many smaller islands, north of Australia.
clue2: It is the most linguistically diverse country in the world, with more than 800 languages.
clue3: Its rainforests are home to many birds-of-paradise, and the Kokoda Track was the site of fierce fighting in World War II.

clue1: It is a Polynesian island nation in the South Pacific, roughly midway between Hawaii and New Zealand.
clue2: In 2011 it jumped across the International Date Line, skipping December 30 entirely.
clue3: The fire-knife dance, known as siva afi, originated here.

clue1: It is a Polynesian archipelago of about 170 islands in the South Pacific, south of Samoa and east of Fiji.
clue2: It was never formally colonized and remains a monarchy today.
clue3: Humpback whales migrate here each year, and visitors can swim alongside them.

clue1: It is an island nation in the western Pacific Ocean, east of the Philippines.
clue2: It created one of the world's first national shark sanctuaries in 2009.
clue3: Jellyfish Lake, where visitors snorkel among stingless jellyfish, and the mushroom-shaped Rock Islands are iconic.

clue1: It is a Y-shaped archipelago of about 80 islands in the South Pacific, west of Fiji and east of Australia.
clue2: It is the birthplace of bungee jumping, which is based on a land-diving ritual on Pentecost Island.
clue3: Mount Yasur on Tanna Island is one of the most accessible active volcanoes in the world.

clue1: It is a tiny island nation in Micronesia in the central Pacific, just south of the equator.
clue2: It is the world's smallest island nation, and its economy once depended heavily on phosphate mining.
clue3: It has no official capital city, though its government offices are in the Yaren district.
